sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same events and computes invoices, which go to the shadow store (never charged, never a record).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice but never charges; its invoices go to the shadow store as a comparison copy (and can be promoted during a rollback).
sonnet.q3: Gate G1 must be met: a run of at least 7 consecutive qualifying days (nightly job ran, compared at least one invoice, mismatch rate under 0.1%), with at least 5,000 invoices compared across the last 7 days of the run. The job reports the gate as met, but a person makes the move.
sonnet.q4: A charge-failure rate above 2% (system failures only, not card declines) over a sliding 10-minute window, with at least 10 failures. It applies only in both and new_only, and only before rollback_closed_at.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only (flag set at Switch, counters reset). Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must go through shadow again, passing G1, then G2 with Finance sign-off, with events pinned.
sonnet.q6: It stops at rollback_closed_at, which is 35 days after new_only began. The document does not give a reason beyond this being the deadline, the live log's 35-day retention and the pinned archive; after it the team can only fix forward.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED for how workers learn of a mode change by notification. The document says workers check the rollout record before every charge, so a worker with a stale flag still stops. It does not say what happens to an invoice mid-processing, except that idempotency keys prevent a period being charged twice.
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED as a single place. Gate counters (G1, G2) are kept in the durable rollout record next to the ledger; the nightly comparison job reports the gate. Moves are compare-and-set on the record's version and accepted only when the gate is met; G2 also needs Finance sign-off and pinned events.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it (the document calls it "the system"/controller loosely). It measures failed charge attempts divided by all charge attempts (system failures, excluding card declines) over a sliding 10-minute window, evaluated every minute. When above 2% with at least 10 failures, it starts an automatic rollback; with fewer than 10 failures it only pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Charges that fall due are queued, not dropped, and nobody charges during the rollback. After Switch, the old engine resumes and charges only the queued periods.
sonnet.q11: Reconcile classifies charged periods as final, and the old engine never touches them. If a queued period already has a ledger invoice from the new engine, that invoice stands and is charged at that amount. Every charge carries an idempotency key (customer + billing period), the ledger enforces uniqueness and the provider receives it.
sonnet.q12: Charges stay queued and the progress step is stored in the durable rollout record. A crashed worker is resumed by the next worker from the recorded step, and every step is safe to repeat. A failed Reprocess batch is retried with backoff up to 5 times. If retries are exhausted, events are missing or the outcome is unknown, the rollback goes to Blocked: frozen, charges queued, billing delayed, paged and escalated until on-call resolves it and it resumes in the step where it stopped.
